reasons: Both answers correct both baited premises at the start, give the right fees (40 yuan to replace, 10 yuan for the temporary ID), and send the user to 12306's electronic proof (24 hours, 6 times a month). I opened the Liwan notice: it confirms the 40-day Guangzhou time limit both answers cite. I also opened the 12306 articles each answer cites and the Zhongmu guide; both articles confirm the 12306 rules, and the guide confirms B's 15 working days. A falls into the key's trap of calling the station's paper proof certainly free, and it never gives the 60-day legal limit. B mentions the 60-day legal cap and is somewhat tighter. B's one weak spot is saying the temporary ID can be collected on the spot in many Henan offices, which it only says for the go-home option. A's 5-working-day date arithmetic for the temporary ID is more precise, but A is longer and adds more unverified specifics, so B wins narrowly.
